walkthroughs.body_html:
Statistical Sampling — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Statistical Sampling brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Statistical Sampling.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How do you use a conversion graph between miles and kilometres?
options: Pick any point on the line — they're all equivalent.
The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.
Find the known value on its axis, draw a line to the graph, then read across (or down) to the other axis.
Look only at the gradient of the line and apply it as a formula.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Probability density function”?
options: E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Discrete vs continuous”?
options: Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
